title: Shopify Design Feasibility — Framework for Reviewing UI Elements
content:
When reviewing a Shopify storefront design, every UI element falls into one of three tiers. Use this framework to communicate feasibility to clients and design teams before development begins.

TIER 1 — NATIVE: Works out of the box in any modern Shopify theme (OS 2.0+). No custom code required. Merchant enables via Theme Editor or Admin. Examples: storefront filtering by availability/price/variants, sort-by dropdown, product recommendations, multi-currency switcher, pagination, breadcrumbs, subscription/selling plan selection, announcement bar, predictive search (results page), collections/search/product templates.

TIER 2 — LIQUID/THEME CODE: Achievable within a custom theme using Liquid templating and targeted JavaScript (under the 16KB budget). Requires a developer but no third-party app. Examples: color swatch filters, active filter chips, price range slider, mega menu, quick-add drawer, sticky add-to-cart bar, video background sections, size guide modal, grid/list toggle, metafield badges, countdown timer, collection empty state.

TIER 3 — CUSTOM/APP: Requires a third-party Shopify app, significant custom JavaScript, or backend integration. Cannot be built within a standard theme alone. Examples: wishlist, back-in-stock notifications, product reviews, compare products, recently viewed (localStorage), bundle builder, gift wrapping, loyalty points, age gate.

FEASIBILITY REVIEW PROCESS: (1) List every distinct UI element or pattern in the design. (2) Classify each as Native / Liquid / Custom. (3) For Custom elements, identify the likely app or implementation approach. (4) Flag any element that conflicts with Shopify hard limits (3 variant options max, 16KB JS budget, no checkout customization without Shopify Plus). (5) Present findings as a feasibility matrix: element name, tier, implementation note, estimated dev effort.

FIGMA IMPLICATION: When reviewing a design file, annotate each section or component with its feasibility tier using Figma's Annotation feature or sticky notes. Use a consistent colour code: green = Native, amber = Liquid, red = Custom/App. Include a feasibility legend frame at the top of each page. In handoff specs, add a 'Feasibility' property to every component: Native | Liquid | Custom(App: [app name]).

title: Shopify Filter & Navigation Elements — Native vs Liquid vs Custom
content:
Detailed feasibility classification for filtering, search, and navigation UI elements.

FILTERING:
— Availability filter (In stock / Out of stock): NATIVE. Built into Storefront Filtering API. Merchant enables in Theme Editor. No code changes needed.
— Price range filter (min/max inputs): LIQUID. Storefront Filtering API provides the data; min/max input fields are standard HTML. Annotate: 'Requires JS to submit filter on input change.'
— Price range slider (visual drag handle): LIQUID. Same API data; slider UI is custom JavaScript. Not a standard HTML element. Budget impact: ~3–5KB JS.
— Multi-select checkbox filters (size, colour, material): LIQUID. Storefront Filtering renders attribute groups; checkboxes are standard HTML. Requires JS to apply filters without full page reload.
— Color swatch filters (circles instead of text): LIQUID. No native swatch renderer. Developer maps option values to hex/image via metafields or hardcoded lookup. Requires custom JS. Always annotate which field drives the colour (e.g., 'product.options[0] = "Color"').
— Active filter chips above product grid: LIQUID. Constructed by reading URL parameters in Liquid and rendering removable pills. Requires JS to handle chip removal.
— Filter result count update: LIQUID. Count comes from `collection.all_products_count` (filtered). Updates on page re-render; real-time AJAX count update requires additional JS.
— Metafield custom filters (e.g., 'Material: Organic Cotton'): NATIVE (OS 2.0). Merchant creates metafield definition in Admin + enables as filter in Theme Editor. No custom code if metafield is a standard type.
— Sort-by dropdown: NATIVE. Query parameter `sort_by` (relevance, price-ascending, price-descending, best-selling, created-at, title-ascending). Annotate: design 6 sort options maximum.
— Filter sidebar (desktop): LIQUID. 240–280px panel, collapsible groups. Standard Liquid section.
— Filter drawer (mobile): LIQUID. Slides in from bottom or right. Requires JS for open/close animation. Standard pattern in Dawn and Horizon.

SEARCH:
— Predictive search with product thumbnails: LIQUID. Uses `/search/suggest.json` endpoint. Requires JS to fetch and render suggestions. Common in all modern themes.
— Search results page with filters: NATIVE. Same Storefront Filtering API applies to search template. Merchant enables in Theme Editor.
— Search with no results empty state: LIQUID. `search.results.size == 0` condition in Liquid; renders static empty state. Pure Liquid, no JS needed.

NAVIGATION:
— Standard header nav (1–3 levels): LIQUID. Three levels of `linklists` nesting. Requires JS for dropdown open/close and keyboard accessibility.
— Mega menu (multi-column dropdown): LIQUID. CSS + JS layout over standard nav data. No new data source; presentation layer only. Budget: ~4–6KB JS for accessibility.
— Hamburger mobile menu: LIQUID. Standard toggle pattern. Requires JS for open/close, focus trap.
— Breadcrumbs: LIQUID. Rendered from page context (collection → product hierarchy). Pure Liquid, no JS needed. Include JSON-LD structured data markup.

FIGMA IMPLICATION: On every filter/navigation frame, add a feasibility annotation chip (Native/Liquid/Custom). For Liquid elements, note the JS requirement and estimated budget impact. For filter groups, annotate which product attribute drives each group (variant option, metafield, tag, availability, price). Design both the sidebar and drawer filter layouts — developers need both for responsive breakpoints.

title: Shopify Product & Collection Page Elements — Native vs Liquid vs Custom
content:
Feasibility classification for product page and collection page UI patterns.

COLLECTION PAGE:
— Product grid: NATIVE. Collection template renders products automatically. Merchant controls columns via settings.
— Grid/list toggle: LIQUID. JS switches CSS class; localStorage persists preference. ~2KB JS.
— Infinite scroll: CUSTOM. Not built-in; requires AJAX pagination library. Adds significant JS weight. Prefer 'Load more' button (Liquid/JS, simpler) over true infinite scroll.
— 'Load more' button: LIQUID. Fetches next paginated page via AJAX and appends to DOM. ~3KB JS. Preferred performance pattern.
— Numbered pagination: NATIVE. Liquid `paginate` tag. Pure Liquid, no JS needed.
— Quick view modal: LIQUID. JS fetches product section HTML and renders in modal. Standard pattern in Horizon/Dawn. ~4KB JS.
— Quick add to cart (button on card): LIQUID. JS posts to `/cart/add.json` without page reload. ~2KB JS. No modal needed.
— Collection empty state: LIQUID. `collection.all_products_count == 0` condition. Pure Liquid.
— Collection image hero banner: NATIVE. Section with `collection.image` object. No code changes needed.

PRODUCT PAGE:
— Product title, price, vendor, SKU: NATIVE. Standard Liquid objects (`product.title`, `product.price`, etc.).
— Strikethrough sale price: NATIVE. `product.compare_at_price > product.price` condition in Liquid.
— Variant selector (dropdown): NATIVE. Standard `<select>` with variant options. JS updates price/image on change.
— Variant selector (pill buttons): LIQUID. Custom rendering instead of native `<select>`. JS state management for selected/unavailable states.
— Color swatches (variant option): LIQUID. Custom rendering from option values + metafield colour mapping. JS required. Annotate: each swatch needs `aria-label`, selected outline, unavailable strikethrough state.
— Product image gallery (thumbnails + main): LIQUID. Standard section pattern. JS for thumbnail click to update main image.
— Product image zoom (click/hover): LIQUID. JS library (medium-zoom or similar). ~5KB.
— Product video (inline, within gallery): NATIVE. Shopify `product.media` supports video type. Renders with native `<video>` element.
— 3D model viewer: NATIVE. Shopify supports `model_viewer` web component for `.glb` files. Requires `<model-viewer>` custom element (loaded by Shopify).
— Sticky add-to-cart bar (scrolled): LIQUID. CSS `position: sticky` + JS scroll listener. ~2KB.
— Selling plan / subscription selector: NATIVE (if merchant has selling plans app). Liquid renders `product.selling_plan_groups`. Requires selling plan app (e.g., Recharge) to be installed.
— Product recommendations (related): NATIVE. `product.related_products` or Recommendations API endpoint. No code changes if section is already in theme.
— Complementary products: NATIVE. `product.complementary_products` via API. Same as above.
— Metafield blocks (care guide, specs): LIQUID. Merchant adds metafield block in Theme Editor; Liquid renders the value. No custom code if block is already in theme.
— Size guide modal/drawer: LIQUID. Static content in a modal triggered by a link. ~2KB JS for modal open/close.
— Recently viewed products: CUSTOM. localStorage-based. JS reads/writes viewed product IDs. No Shopify API — entirely client-side. ~4KB JS.
— Back-in-stock notification: CUSTOM/APP. Requires third-party app (e.g., Klaviyo, Back in Stock). No native support.
— Product reviews (stars, form): CUSTOM/APP. No native reviews. App block required (Yotpo, Judge.me, Loox, Shopify Product Reviews).
— Bundle builder: CUSTOM/APP. No native bundle support. Third-party app required.
— Wishlist / save for later: CUSTOM/APP. No native wishlist. App or custom JS + customer metafield storage.
— Compare products: CUSTOM. No native compare. Custom JS + localStorage or app.

FIGMA IMPLICATION: On product and collection frames, add a feasibility legend. Flag any Custom/App element with a red annotation and name the likely app integration. For Liquid elements, add JS budget estimates in the dev notes. For Native elements, confirm the merchant has the required data set up (e.g., metafield definitions created in Admin, selling plan app installed, collection image uploaded).

title: Shopify Global & Checkout UX Elements — Native vs Liquid vs Custom
content:
Feasibility classification for global site patterns, checkout, and marketing elements.

GLOBAL PATTERNS:
— Announcement bar (static text): NATIVE. Standard Liquid section. No JS needed.
— Announcement bar (marquee/scrolling): LIQUID. CSS `@keyframes` or JS scroll animation. ~1KB.
— Announcement bar (dismissible with X): LIQUID. JS sets localStorage flag to hide. ~1KB.
— Multi-currency switcher: NATIVE. Shopify Markets/multi-currency built-in. Liquid `{{shop.enabled_currencies}}`. Merchant enables in Admin.
— Language/locale switcher: NATIVE. Shopify `request.locale` object. Liquid renders locale selector. Merchant enables markets in Admin.
— Country picker with geo-redirect: LIQUID. Liquid `request.locale` + JS redirect logic. No automatic redirect (accessibility: never auto-redirect users).
— Cookie consent banner: CUSTOM/APP. No native Shopify cookie management. Third-party app or custom JS required. Check: Shopify does not handle GDPR compliance natively.
— Age verification gate: CUSTOM. JS modal + localStorage/cookie to persist. No native support. ~3KB JS.
— Countdown timer (promotional): LIQUID. JS setInterval updates DOM every second. ~2KB JS. Pure client-side.
— Sticky header (scroll-activated): LIQUID. CSS `position: sticky` or JS scroll class toggle. ~1KB.
— Back-to-top button: LIQUID. JS scroll listener + CSS transition. ~1KB.
— Live chat widget: CUSTOM/APP. Third-party integration (Tidio, Gorgias, Zendesk). App block or script tag.
— Popups (newsletter, exit-intent): CUSTOM/APP. Third-party app (Privy, Klaviyo) or custom JS. Complex behaviour requires app.
— Loyalty points display: CUSTOM/APP. Third-party loyalty app (Smile.io, LoyaltyLion). No native feature.

CHECKOUT:
— Checkout page layout customization: NATIVE (Shopify Plus only). Standard Shopify: checkout is locked. Cannot add custom sections, blocks, or Liquid to checkout without Shopify Plus + Checkout Extensibility.
— Gift wrapping option: CUSTOM/APP. Line item property on product page (LIQUID, ~1KB), but checkout display requires app or Shopify Plus.
— Order notes field: NATIVE. Cart note via `{{ cart.note }}`. Merchant enables in Theme Editor. Appears in cart, not checkout.
— Custom fields at checkout: NATIVE (Plus). Checkout Extensibility (UI Extensions) required for custom form fields in checkout.
— Post-purchase upsell: CUSTOM/APP. Third-party app (ReConvert, Frequently Bought Together). Not available in standard checkout.

MARKETING & SOCIAL PROOF:
— 'X people viewing this': CUSTOM/APP. No native feature. Third-party urgency app required.
— Social sharing buttons: LIQUID. Static links with query-string sharing to Twitter/Facebook/Pinterest. No JS needed.
— Instagram/UGC feed: CUSTOM/APP. Third-party app or Instagram API integration. No native embed.
— Trust badges (icons + text): LIQUID. Static HTML section with icon + text blocks. No JS needed.
— 'Free shipping over $X' progress bar: LIQUID. JS compares cart total to threshold, animates progress. ~2KB JS.

SHOPIFY-SPECIFIC HARD LIMITS (design must never exceed these):
— 3 variant options maximum per product (e.g., Size + Color + Material). Cannot design a 4th option natively.
— 100 variants per product maximum (combinations of options).
— 3 levels of navigation nesting maximum (menus go no deeper).
— 16KB JavaScript budget for theme JS (minified). Each custom feature eats into this.
— Checkout is locked on standard Shopify — no custom layout, sections, or blocks in checkout without Plus.
— No server-side logic beyond Liquid — cannot call external APIs in Liquid templates (use AJAX or app proxy).

FIGMA IMPLICATION: For any checkout-adjacent design, annotate 'Shopify Plus required' if it involves checkout customization. For third-party app elements, annotate the app name and note that the design is an approximation — final rendering is controlled by the app's embed script. For cart pages, note that Order Notes is a native feature but gift wrapping requires app integration.
